moat_against: No demonstrated returns on capital: roic_proxy in fundamentals.json is negative every year FY2021-FY2025 (-5.3% to -27.9%) and owner's earnings are negative in 0 of the last 5 years

Reimbursement is the moat's weak wall: Medicare Administrative Contractor coverage for iDose TR is still being settled, the Epioxa J-code transition was guided to cause Q3 2026 volatility, and MIGS reimbursement cuts have reduced procedure volumes before

Competition from much larger ophthalmology players: Alcon (Hydrus Microstent), Sight Sciences (OMNI), AbbVie (XEN Gel Stent), plus drops and laser as the default alternatives; management itself bakes combo-cataract MIGS competition abroad into guidance

Dilution funds the franchise: SBC rose $43,528,000 (FY2023) to $63,218,000 (FY2025) to $80,222,000 (TTM), and the diluted count compounds at 6.4%/yr (48,433,000 in FY2023 to 58,419,000 current-YTD 2026), so any future OE is divided by a growing count
Concentration and execution: growth now hinges on the iDose TR ramp and the Epioxa launch while operating expenses are guided to ~$600M for 2026 — GAAP losses continue by design until scale arrives
moat_for: Interventional-glaucoma category leadership: iStent family is the largest MIGS franchise (over one million devices implanted worldwide, deep peer-reviewed evidence base), iStent infinite extends it to standalone use
iDose TR — first sustained-release intracameral drug implant for glaucoma, with re-administration creating a recurring-revenue refill model; ~$74M of Q2 2026 sales, U.S. glaucoma +64% YoY
Epioxa — first FDA-approved epithelium-on corneal cross-linking therapy for keratoconus; ~$11M in its first full quarter (Q2 2026) with a permanent J-code effective July 1, 2026
Pricing power in the filed numbers: GAAP gross margin 76.0% (FY2023) / 75.5% (FY2024), non-GAAP ~84% (FY2025) and ~85% (Q2 2026) as iDose/Epioxa mix rises

Pipeline breadth beyond one product: five platforms / 13 programs (iDose TREX and TRIO, next-gen iLink, PRESERFLO, retinal wet-AMD program) plus a trained surgeon base that is costly for rivals to replicate
moat_justification: Category creator and leader in interventional glaucoma: the iStent family holds the largest MIGS share with over one million devices implanted and a deep clinical-evidence base, iDose TR is the first sustained-release intracameral travoprost implant (re-administration makes it recurring), and Epioxa is the first FDA-approved epithelium-on corneal cross-linking therapy for keratoconus. Pricing power is in the filed numbers: GAAP gross margin 76.0% (FY2023) and 75.5% (FY2024) in fundamentals.json, and ~84% non-GAAP in FY2025 (the GAAP 55.7% is a one-time $112.9M non-cash Avedro intangible impairment, not price erosion). But there is no demonstrated return on capital: the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json is negative in every year FY2021-FY2025 (-5.34%, -15.84%, -27.61%, -16.18%, -27.89%) and conservative owner's earnings are negative in 0 of the last 5 years. The franchise is hostage to Medicare coverage/reimbursement decisions, faces Alcon/Sight Sciences/AbbVie competition, and pays for growth with rising SBC ($63,218,000 in FY2025, $80,222,000 TTM). A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years.
name: Glaukos Corporation
one_liner: Category-leading interventional-glaucoma franchise (iStent / iDose TR) plus the Epioxa launch, moat 5/10 — but owner's earnings are negative in all of the last 5 years (normalized base -$2.23/share; FY2025 -$1.50/share and TTM -$1.58/share, because SBC of $63,218,000 in FY2025 and $80,222,000 TTM sits on top of negative-to-breakeven operating cash flow) — Tier F on this screen; it does not clear 15% at any price on current numbers and no hurdle-clearing price is computed on a negative base. The 2026 ramp (Q2 sales +50% YoY, guidance raised to $680M-$700M) is a re-rating story, not yet an owner's-earnings story.
sector: Healthcare / Ophthalmic medical technology & pharmaceuticals (interventional glaucoma, corneal health)
